title: Specify per-link hop and time context
description:
Specify a proposed per-link sequence and time context bound to identities, block ID, plan/version, profile and schedule generation. Define phase progression when fragments are absent, uncertainty bounds, sparse allowed sets, wrap behavior and conflicts at a shared half-duplex receiver.

HPC8 execution policy: Code, test, or schema changes require three independent correctness, security, and robustness reviews; file and fix all findings and re-review. Use independent oracles, never weakened legacy tests or self-generated expected results. Preserve upstream Yggdrasil addressing, radio-owned identity, best-effort custody, baseline SCHC, and the human-only OSCORE/EDHOC security edit bar. External actions, hardware/RF operations, and port access require scoped explicit permission and applicable bench safety checks. Research may conclude no-go; an authorization gate requires affirmative, recorded approval for its actual scope. Dependency closure and decomposition are not permission. No speculative activation, including deferred portability or experimental modes.
design: Proposal only, using adopted CCP2 semantics. Do not allocate wire bits or activate a profile. Final integration must use wire.12 and vectors.11; authentication and experimental code approval are separate microfrag.06 decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Independent preimage/byte examples and event tables show loss-independent phase advancement and bounded resynchronization. Network-wide lockstep is not counted as parallel per-link reception. Identify receiver commitments and complete-operation limits without claiming a deterministic hash establishes legal hopping.
